input: boxes is an Array of n integer colors in [1,100], with 0 <= n <=100. Empty input is an explicit extension. Integer inputs, when present, are primitive safe-integer Numbers excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt. Arrays are dense ordinary Arrays without holes, proxies, subclasses or accessors; strings are primitive. No concurrent mutation or modified standard built-ins are allowed. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Size bounds do not guarantee available memory or completion within an unqualified runtime budget.
return: The exact maximum score from repeatedly removing a nonempty contiguous equal-color group, earning the square of that group size, until no boxes remain. Removal joins the remaining sides. Empty input returns 0. The method returns score, not a deletion order.
mutation_aliasing: All input values, caller containers and ordering remain unchanged. The Solution instance retains no state and separate calls share no mutable result state. The removal game is modeled through interval states; boxes is not shortened, reordered or marked. A private memo retains integer scores only.
numeric: Scores and every candidate sum are bounded by n*n <=10000 because a state partitions at most n original boxes into disjoint removed groups. joined counts at most n-1 same-color boxes retained outside the active interval. Indices, counts, squares and sums remain exact safe integers. Recursion shrinks the active interval at each call, so at most n+1 <=101 calls are live.
complexity: O(n^4+1) memoized time and O(n^3+1) memo storage plus O(n+1) recursive stack, assuming average constant map operations. At most O(n^3) raw (left,right,joined) states are evaluated; each scans/compresses at most O(n) positions. The raw-state memo lookup occurs BEFORE trailing-run normalization, so cached calls do not rescan. Python keys are three-integer tuples; JavaScript keys are three comma-delimited nonnegative integers, at most 8 characters for this domain, and their construction is charged. Map/set operation costs assume ordinary average O(1) lookup; target-runtime behavior must be qualified, and universal ECMAScript constant-time guarantees or adversarial collision resistance are not claimed.

helpers.name: score
helpers.contract: For interval [left,right] with joined additional boxes matching its rightmost color, maximize the removal score. Memoize the raw incoming state; coalesce its equal suffix; either remove that group now or retain it to merge with an earlier equal-color box after removing the intervening interval.
